sections.heading: Abhishek Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 January, 2016
content: This petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C against the order dated 27.6.2012. By the aforesaid order the trial court accepted the compromise filed by the parties in regard to commission of offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC. However, the trila court refused to accept the compromise in regard to commission of offence punishable under Section 66-C and 66-D of the Technology Act.

The allegation against the applicant was that he received ATM Card of the complainant and also got information about code number of the ATM card and thereafter he had withdrawn an amount of Rs.17700 from the account of Sonam Sharma through ATM Card by using facility of Internet bank. During the pendendy of the application the complainant filed an application for compromise. The permission was also granted. however the trial court refused to grant permission for compromise in regard to commission of offence punishable under Section 66-C and 66-D of the Information and Technology Act on the ground that no compromise is permissible for commission of offence punishable under the aforesaid Sections.

The question which now remains to be answered is whether since the offences punishable under Sections 66- C & 66- D of Information Technology Act are not compoundable, the proceedings of complaint case could be quashed.
It is pertinent to mention here that dispute between the parties is of private nature and having no adverse effect to others and presently it is resolved also.
The Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another 2012 AIR SCW 5333 considered the relevant provisions of the Code and concluded as under:-

Since the parties had buried the hatchet by amicably settling their disputes, this Court could allow the matter to be compounded. In the totality of the circumstances, I am of the view that the compromise settlement arrived at between the parties in form of compromise petition is a sensible step that will benefit the parties. Continuation of criminal proceeding would amount to abuse of process of law. There is no possibility of conviction in view of compromise entered between the parties. In this view of the matter, the petition filed by the petitioner is allowed. The impugned order passed by the trial court and the order passed by the revisional court are hereby set aside. The application for compromise is hereby allowed. The applicant is acquitted from the charges punishable under Sections 204 , 66-C and 66-D of the of the Technology Act.
